record.paper_title: Variation Structures: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Consider composed germs f=p∘ϕ, where ϕ:(C^{n+2},0)->(C^2,0) has discriminant Δ and p:(C^2,0)->(C,0) is a reduced irreducible curve singularity. The signature σ(f) can be expressed through contributions from the splice diagram of p^{-1}(0)∪Δ, and abelian variation-structure data over a Seifert component can be computed from eta-invariants of V(ϕ). Which composed germs f=p∘ϕ have the stronger property that σ(f) can be computed only from the eta-invariant η_{V(ϕ)} and the curve singularity p?

evidence.quote: Our goal is to compute σ(f ). For simplicity, assume that p is reduced and irreducible. Consider the splice diagram Γ(p, ∆) of the multilink determined by p−1 (0)∪ ∆ ⊂ (C2 , 0), where the multiplicity of p−1 (0) is 1, and the other multiplicities are zero.
Theorem.[13] The signature σ(f ) is a sum σ(f ) = nodes σ(Σ, ρ) over the nodes of Γ(p, ∆)
(b) If the variation structure above Σ is abelian, then: σ(Σ, ρ) = ∑r 1=1 ni · η(Li mi/ni Mi m′i/ni ).
Problem # 10. Characterize composed germs f = p ◦ ϕ such that σ(f ) can be computed only in terms of ηV(ϕ) and p.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\phi:(\mathbb{C}^{n+2},0)\to(\mathbb{C}^2,0)$ be a holomorphic map germ with isolated critical points and discriminant curve $\Delta\subset(\mathbb{C}^2,0)$, and let $p:(\mathbb{C}^2,0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ be a reduced irreducible plane curve singularity. Consider the composed germ $f=p\circ\phi:(\mathbb{C}^{n+2},0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$, with Milnor fiber $F_f$ and signature $\sigma(f):=\mathrm{sign}(F_f)$ defined via the intersection form on the middle cohomology.

To $\phi$ one associates its Hermitian variation structure $V(\phi)$ (a tuple $(H;b,h,V)$ consisting of the intersection form $b$, the algebraic monodromy $h$ and the variation map $V$ on the middle cohomology of the Milnor fiber). From this data one defines the eta-invariant $\eta_{V(\phi)}$, a function $S^1\setminus\{1\}\to\mathbb{Q}$ encoding, via the spectral decomposition of $V(\phi)$ over each eigenspace of $h$, the Atiyah–Patodi–Singer eta-contributions associated with $V(\phi)$.

It is known that, using the splice diagram $\Gamma(p,\Delta)$ of the multilink $p^{-1}(0)\cup\Delta\subset(\mathbb{C}^2,0)$ (with $p^{-1}(0)$ given multiplicity $1$ and components of $\Delta$ multiplicity $0$), the signature decomposes as a sum of local contributions $\sigma(\Sigma,\rho)$ over the nodes of $\Gamma(p,\Delta)$, and that over a node whose Seifert piece $\Sigma$ carries an abelian variation structure, this contribution is expressible as a sum $\sum_{i=1}^{r} n_i\,\eta\!\left(\tfrac{L_i^{m_i/n_i}}{M_i^{m'_i/n_i}}\right)$ of values of $\eta_{V(\phi)}$ at roots of unity determined by splice-diagram weights.

Problem. Characterize precisely those composed germs $f=p\circ\phi$ for which the signature $\sigma(f)$ can be computed using only the eta-invariant $\eta_{V(\phi)}$ together with the curve singularity $p$ (i.e., without further data from the splice diagram of $p^{-1}(0)\cup\Delta$ or from non-abelian variation contributions at the nodes).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the survey on variation structures and is not addressed by the closely related works on eta-invariants of variation structures (Némethi), rho-invariants of iterated torus knots (Borodzik), or the slope/signature formulas for splices of links. No publication characterizing the composed germs with the requested property was located.

status_evidence.title: The eta-invariant of variation structures I
status_evidence.snippet: Defines and studies the eta-invariant attached to a Hermitian variation structure; does not characterize composed germs whose signature is determined by eta and p alone.
status_evidence.claim: Background result on eta-invariants, not addressing the characterization question.

status_evidence.title: A rho-invariant of iterated torus knots (Borodzik)
status_evidence.snippet: Computes signature/rho contributions for splice diagrams of iterated torus knots; uses node-by-node decomposition rather than reducing all data to eta of V(phi) and p.
status_evidence.claim: Related computational framework but does not give the asked characterization.

status_evidence.title: Slopes of links and signature formulas
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces slope invariants and completes signature formulas for splices of links.
status_evidence.claim: Provides general splice signature formulas, not a characterization of composed germs reducing to eta_{V(phi)} and p.
